deadline.value: The priority deadline is January 15, but the page gives no year, so no Fall 2027 date is recorded.
deadline.quote: The priority deadline for applications is January 15 at 11:59 p.m. (EST)

gre_subject.value: The subject GRE is not required but may be considered if you submit it.
gre_subject.quote: The physics subject GRE is not a requirement, but may be considered as part of your application if you choose to provide it

gre_general.value: The department says its GRE requirement has been eliminated.
gre_general.quote: The GRE Requirement has been eliminated for admission to the FSU Department of Physics graduate program

toefl_min.value: The department asks for an Internet TOEFL of 80, an old-scale figure; the Graduate School's current rule is 4.0 on the new scale, so confirm which scale applies.
toefl_min.quote: with a minimum score of 550 on the paper-based test, 213 on the computer-based test, and 80 on the Internet-based test

also.quote: Internet based TOEFL (IBTOEFL): 80 (if taken before January 21, 2026) or 4.0 (if taken on or after January 21, 2026)

supervisor.value: The department pages do not say whether a faculty supervisor must agree before admission.

funding.value: Every admitted doctoral student receives a funding package covering at least five years.
funding.quote: All students admitted to the Doctoral Program in Physics receive a funding package, which covers a minimum of five years

entry_route.value: The University minimum accepts a bachelor's or a graduate degree; the department page adds no rule.
entry_route.quote: A bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited U.S. institution, or a comparable degree from an international institution | A graduate degree from a regionally accredited U.S. institution, or a comparable degree from an international institution

notes: Funding: TA in the first two semesters, then a research group. Department FAQ and How to Apply pages dated 2025-07-23. Department says the Graduate School cannot waive the application fee; the Graduate School page allows narrow exceptions.
